vocabulary.meaningInContext: bombs (explosive devices); here, the destruction Jimmy plants flowers amid

examples.text: Les bombes ont détruit la ville.

vocabulary.meaningInContext: to grow; in 'faire pousser', to make (flowers) grow

morphology.description: infinitive of 'pousser' (to push / to grow); here governed by 'faire' (causative)

vocabulary.meaningInContext: heart (the emotional seat); note the œ spelling
collocations: avoir le cœur brisé (to have a broken heart)

examples.text: Je t'aime de tout mon cœur.
examples.translation: I love you with all my heart.

vocabulary.meaningInContext: weapons / arms; 'le choix des armes' = the choice of weapons

morphology.description: plural of 'une arme' (feminine, even though it denotes a weapon)

vocabulary.meaningInContext: the child ('l'enfant': the article is elided before the vowel)

morphology.description: definite article 'le' elided to l' before the vowel-initial noun 'enfant'

vocabulary.meaningInContext: tears; 'n'a plus de larmes' = has no tears left

confusions.distinction: tears vs. weapons — a near-homophone the song itself plays on

vocabulary.meaningInContext: travels (present, 3rd person singular of 'voyager'); 'Jimmy voyage' = Jimmy travels
notes: Same spelling as the noun 'le voyage' (the journey) — see v009.

vocabulary.meaningInContext: journey / trip; 'C'est un voyage' = it's a journey

confusions.distinction: 'le voyage' (journey) vs. 'il voyage' (he travels) — identical spelling, different part of speech

vocabulary.meaningInContext: detour; 'vaut bien le détour' = is well worth the detour

examples.text: Nous avons fait un détour par la côte.
examples.translation: We made a detour along the coast.

vocabulary.meaningInContext: rains; 'faire revenir les pluies' = to make the rains return

morphology.description: plural of 'la pluie' (rain); plural used here for repeated rains

vocabulary.meaningInContext: earth / land / ground; here the land that yields nothing

confusions.distinction: 'solitaire' stresses the isolated temperament; 'seul' is the plain word for 'alone'

vocabulary.meaningInContext: border / frontier; 'n'a pas de frontière' = has no borders (nothing limits him)
notes: Echoes 'sans frontières' (without borders), as in Médecins Sans Frontières.

vocabulary.meaningInContext: advance / move forward (present, 3rd person plural of 'avancer'; describes the clouds)

morphology.description: 3rd-person plural present of 'avancer' (the -c- takes a cedilla before -a: 'avancent')

expressions.literalMeaning: At the four corners of the world
expressions.meaningInContext: everywhere / in all corners of the world

examples.text: On vend ce produit aux quatre coins du monde.
examples.translation: This product is sold in every corner of the world.

expressions.text: Loin des yeux, près du cœur
expressions.literalMeaning: Far from the eyes, near to the heart
expressions.meaningInContext: a twist on 'loin des yeux, loin du cœur' (out of sight, out of mind): here the opposite — distant but still close in feeling
usageNotes: Plays on the common proverb 'loin des yeux, loin du cœur' (out of sight, out of mind) by inverting it.

expressions.meaningInContext: has no choice (avoir le choix = to have the choice)
plays tricks (on him); 'jouer des tours à quelqu'un' = to play tricks on someone

examples.text: Ma mémoire me joue des tours.
examples.translation: My memory is playing tricks on me.

expressions.meaningInContext: is well worth the detour (valoir le détour = to be worth the detour)

examples.translation: This village is worth the detour.

expressions.meaningInContext: backlit (photography term); figuratively, living in the shadows, unnoticed or against the current
usageNotes: Literally a lighting term (a subject photographed against the light). Figuratively it suggests people who live out of view or against the grain.

grammar.title: faire + infinitive — the causative
grammar.explanation: 'faire' + infinitive means 'to make/have something happen'. 'Fait pousser des fleurs' = makes flowers grow; 'Fait revenir les pluies' = makes the rains come back. Jimmy causes the action; he does not do the growing/returning himself.

examples.translation: She is having the car repaired.

pitfalls: using the wrong pronoun for the doer of the action

grammar.title: Negation — ne … pas / ne … plus (de)
grammar.explanation: French negation frames the verb with 'ne' before it and 'pas' or 'plus' after: 'n'a pas' (has not), 'n'a plus' (has no longer). Before an object, 'ne … plus de' loses the article: 'n'a plus de larmes' (has no more tears), 'ne donne plus de fruits' (no longer bears fruit). The text's 'ne donne plus de fruits' is the negated form of the collocation 'donner des fruits' (to bear fruit).
grammar.pattern: ne + verb + pas / plus (+ de + noun)
pitfalls: forgetting 'ne' in speech (the written text keeps it)

grammar.title: au bout de + noun — 'at the end of'
grammar.explanation: 'au bout de' (= à + le + bout de) means 'at the end of / to the end of', used for both space and time. 'Au bout de l'amour' = to the end of love — the destination of Jimmy's journey.
grammar.pattern: au bout de + noun (à + le → au)

examples.text: Il attend au bout de la rue.
examples.translation: He is waiting at the end of the street.

examples.text: Au bout d'un moment, il est parti.

pitfalls: using 'à la fin de' where 'au bout de' (extent) is meant

grammar.title: même si + indicative — 'even if'
grammar.explanation: 'même si' introduces a concession and takes the indicative (not the subjunctive): 'même si ça lui joue des tours' = even if it plays tricks on him. Compare 'bien que' (although), which takes the subjunctive.

examples.translation: Even if it rains, I'm going out.
Although it is raining, I'm going out.

exercises.prompt: What does « Aux quatre coins du monde » mean?
options: everywhere / in all corners of the world
the four corners of a room

answer.key: everywhere / in all corners of the world
answer.explanation: It is a fixed expression meaning 'everywhere'.

exercises.prompt: Complete the line: Fait pousser des fleurs sous les {{blank}}.

answer.explanation: 'sous les bombes' = under the bombs — the war imagery of the first stanza.

exercises.prompt: In « fait pousser des fleurs », what does the « faire + infinitive » construction mean?

answer.explanation: 'faire' + infinitive is the causative: the subject causes the action.

exercises.prompt: Translate into English: « Jimmy voyage au bout de l'amour ».

answer.model: Jimmy travels to the end of love.
rubric: renders 'au bout de' as 'to the end of'
answer.explanation: 'au bout de' = to the end of; 'voyage' here is the verb (voyager).

exercises.prompt: « Loin des yeux, près du cœur » inverts a common proverb. What does it mean here?
options: distant but still close in feeling

answer.key: distant but still close in feeling
answer.explanation: It flips 'loin des yeux, loin du cœur' (out of sight, out of mind) to say the opposite.

exercises.prompt: In « il n'a plus de larmes », what does « ne … plus » mean?

answer.explanation: 'ne … plus' = no longer; 'ne … plus de' drops the article before the noun.
